title: Technical qualification storyboard — rapid iteration
content:
Slide 1 — One-line objective
- Purpose: give field engineers and AE/SE pairs a lightweight, repeatable technical qualification flow for platform-led closes. Keep it <10 mins for first pass.
Speaker note: start with why we ask these things (latency/cost/ops constraints).

Slide 2 — TL;DR qualification checklist (what we need to know fast)
- Customer persona: product team / platform team / AI-narrow vendor
- Key SLO: p95 latency target (ms) and throughput (reqs/s)
- Data sensitivity: PII/PHI? On-prem/VPC required?
- Scale expectation: steady QPS and expected spikes (x baseline)
- Deployment constraint: cloud regions, private infra, air-gap?
- Budget signal: token budget or reserved capacity target

Slide 3 — Quick demo script (5 minutes)
- 0:00 Intro + ask: "what's a realistic sample workload?"
- 0:30 Show model catalog and 2 candidate variants (base & quantized)
- 1:15 Run a 3-turn chat example, show latency and token count meter
- 2:15 Toggle batching settings and simulate burst to show SLO impact
- 3:00 Show rollout plan snippet (canary -> 50% -> 100%)
- 4:00 Show cost estimate widget for hosted vs dedicated
Speaker note: keep it interactive — ask them to give a sample prompt they actually use.

Slide 4 — Fast-tech checklist for SEs (copyable)
- Ask for representative prompt set (5–20 samples)
- Ask for typical sequence lengths and max length
- Confirm inference mode: streaming vs full response
- Confirm multi-turn cache needs (preserve KV between requests?)
- Check if custom tooling/functions required
- Confirm compliance: audit log retention, KMS, VPC peering

Slide 5 — Objections and short technical scripts (rebuttals)
- "We can’t change our infra" -> show Private deployment options + minimal footprint on-prem reference
- "Latency is non-negotiable" -> demo lower-latency model variants + routing to dedicated pools
- "Cost is too high" -> show batching/caching + quantization uplift estimates with numbers

Slide 6 — Simple ROI worked example (two scenarios)
- Scenario A: Hosted API, 1M tokens/month, 15% caching -> monthly $X (ballpark)
- Scenario B: Reserved Dedicated 8-GPU pool, steady QPS -> monthly commit $Y, break-even in Z months
Speaker note: use our cost widget during demo; call out assumptions. Include link to Cost playbook.

Slide 7 — Deployment decision map (one-slide flow)
- If PII & compliance -> Private
- If predictable high throughput & low latency -> Dedicated
- If early proof / rapid dev -> Hosted
Notes: this is intentionally simple. Use product console to surface the path.

Slide 8 — Live troubleshooting checklist (for PoC)
- Observe 95th percentile latency, token utilization, error rate
- If p95 > target: reduce batch window, increase dedicated capacity, or pick lower-latency model
- If cost too high: enable prefix caching, lower temperature, quantize where acceptable
- If errors: collect server-side logs, capture request id, escalate to eng-sre with capture link

Slide 9 — Appendix: commands & hints for SEs (copy into Slack)
- Quick curl sample (hosted): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer XXX' -d '{"model":"redwood-xxl","prompt":"..."}'
- Canary rollout snippet: feature_flag=canary; route=10%; fallback=base-model
- Monitoring checklist: add token-cost, latency-per-route, model-fallback count to dashboard

Slide 10 — Notes to self / open questions
- Should we add a tiny one-pager for procurement (reserved vs burst pricing)? PR for cost numbers pending (jira:GT-1662).
- Open: quick legal blurb for international data residency — ask privacy counsel.
- TODO: record a 3-min video demo and attach link to this deck.

Slide X — Speaker cues & cadence tips
- Start by asking for the sample prompt; contextualize the demo to their workload
- Keep transitions tight; call out specific numbers (ms, qps, $)
- Close with next-step checklist: sample prompt set, decision on deployment mode, follow-up SRE call

Backchannel references: Slack thread #go-to-market-demo, confluence/eng/qualification-scripts, github/pr/782-demo-notes

Revision history: 0.1 draft (Aisha) -> 0.2 added ROI example (Carlos) -> 0.3 in_review (Jin)

Open items for reviewers: add one template email for procurement, confirm cost assumptions, sanity-check PII checklist with security team.
